title: A Borrowed Name

source.quote: What is still useful cannot be borrowed; what is of no use — that is what you borrow.

moral: A name everyone knows can gather a scattered crowd again.

story.title: The Group Scatters
story.text: The group scattered, and only one old flag was left.
story.narration: In 209 BC heavy rain trapped the men marching to the frontier at Daze Township. One after another they slipped away, until only an old flag lay in the mud of the camp.

story.title: The Old Flag Goes Up
story.text: The old flag went up, and footsteps came back from every direction.
story.narration: Chen Sheng and Wu Guang raised the old flag, and on it they wrote names everyone knew in their hearts — Fusu and Xiang Yan. Hearing those names, the men who had scattered in every direction came back, one by one.

keyMoment.question: Everyone has scattered. How do you call them back?

options.text: Chase after them one by one
options.hint: They ran in every direction; one person cannot catch them all.
They are still there; they just need a reason to come back.

keyMoment.reveal: A name everyone knows can gather a scattered crowd again.

misconceptions: Once people run off, they can never be called back
The only way to gather people is to fetch them one by one

quiz.question: Whose names did Chen Sheng and Wu Guang borrow?
quiz.explanation: Fusu and Xiang Yan were names people already trusted — with them on the old flag, the men came back.

quiz.question: You want to organize a class activity, but nobody answers when you call. What do you do?
options: Borrow a name everyone knows, like "the class team for the school games"
Pull people in one by one, and give up if they refuse
quiz.explanation: People come for the name they trust. Borrow a reason everyone recognizes, and they gather on their own.
